# GSN Model Architecture Components

Also called: Locally Conditioned Radiance Fields

## Overview
[GSN](#16709-global-scene-generator-gsn.md) (Generative Scene Network) decomposes a scene into many independent locally conditioned radiance fields to improve generative performance over [global conditioning](#12589-global-conditioning.md) methods like [GRAF](#8539-graf.md) [S1]. It distinguishes itself by using modulated linear layers in the generator and a local latent code representation $W \in \mathbb{R}^{c \times s \times s}$, whereas GRAF uses global conditioning with standard linear layers and $\pi$-GAN uses modulated sine layers [S1].

## Shared principles
The core mechanism of GSN is the [decomposition](#7254-decomposition.md) of the scene representation into a grid of local radiance fields, each conditioned by a local latent code.

**Local Latent Code Representation**
Instead of a single global latent vector $w \in \mathbb{R}^c$ that conditions the entire radiance field $f_\theta$, GSN uses a local latent grid $W \in \mathbb{R}^{c \times s \times s}$ [S1]. This decomposition allows the scene to be modeled as many independent locally conditioned radiance fields, which drastically improves generative performance (e.g., reducing FID from 68.42 to 41.75 and SwAV-FID from 6.14 to 4.14 in [ablation studies](#14949-component-ablation-diagnostics.md)) [S1].

**Local Coordinate System and Feature Sharing**
Each local radiance field operates within its own local coordinate system [S1]. This design enables feature sharing: a latent code $w_{ij}$ at grid position $(i, j)$ can represent the same semantic scene part regardless of its absolute position in the global grid [S1]. This robustness is validated by rigidly rearranging latent codes via [2D rotation](#3357-2d-rotation.md); models with local coordinate systems maintain lower FID scores under rearrangement compared to global coordinate systems [S1].

**[Camera Pose Normalization](#7056-bounding-sphere-estimation.md)**
Camera poses are normalized relative to the middle frame of a sub-sequence during training [S1]. This enforces an egocentric coordinate system with the origin at the center of the scene, ensuring consistent spatial relationships across different viewpoints [S1].

**Generator Network Architecture**
The radiance field generator in GSN utilizes modulated linear layers [S1]. This contrasts with GRAF, which uses standard linear layers, and $\pi$-GAN, which employs modulated sine layers [S1]. All compared models use the same base architecture and [training pipeline](#5325-training-pipeline.md) to ensure fair comparison [S1].

## Subtopics

## Background
GSN was introduced in the paper "Unconstrained Scene Generation with Locally Conditioned Radiance Fields" [S1]. The method was developed to address limitations in global conditioning approaches for generative modeling of radiance fields. It was evaluated on unconstrained scene generation tasks where an interactive agent explores scenes, collecting RGB, depth, and camera pose data [S1]. Performance was measured using Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) and SwAV-FID metrics, sampling 5,000 real and 5,000 generated images for evaluation [S1].
